pages.name: Freight Cargo
pages.html:
Travellers are frequently employed to haul freight for companies, governments, and other employers to other systems as a means to make passive income on their travels through space. Unused cargo space will always be of value to someone looking to move product. The character will be offered to transport a large quantity of cargo in their cargo hold to another planet. Station, or other assigned destination at 1000cr per ton. The referee will determine the destination of the delivery and distance needed for the character to travel.

  • Generating amount of cargo: There will be a number of shipments available equal to the destination's population code. For each shipment, roll 1D and multiply it by 5 tonnes. This will represent the size of each shipment type. The referee will determine the trade goods of each shipment. Shipments cannot be broken down into smaller sections.
  • Example: A starport has a job for bringing shipments to a planet with a population code of 5. There are 5 separate types of trade goods being shipped, where each weighs 1D x 5 tonnes. The referee rolls a 5, representing 25 tonnes of medical supplies. The character cannot split up the cargo shipment into a small quantity and must either accept the 25 tonnes or not accept the job.

Book p.62

pages.name: Mail
pages.html:
Information is considered one of the most important commodities, to maintain the function of civilization. This also makes it perfect for hijacking and ransoming back to the sender. If the character has a contract to deliver mail, they will always transport mail to the destination they embark to.

A character can deliver mail if they meet certain criteria:

  • Dedicated cargo space: A ship must reserve 5 tonnes of cargo space that cannot be occupied by anything else, even if they aren’t transporting 5 tonnes of cargo. It is considered rented space to the employing company or government.
  • Properly equipped starship: Mail can only be delivered by an armed starship with a fully trained crew.
  • Proper background: The ship-owning character must have a background in the Merchant or Scout service.
  • Negotiations: Contract negotiations require a 10+, or 6+ if the ship is subsidised to be hired. Each contract lasts one year, with an option to renegotiate.

Every mail delivery will always pay 25,000cr upon delivery regardless of distance travelled.

Book p.62

pages.name: Passengers
pages.html:
A ship with spare staterooms to house passengers can charge room and board to transport people between star systems. Ships will need to have the appropriate accommodations for each type of passage before offering it to potential passengers. Any passengers found are interested in travelling to your planned destination.

  • High Passage: 10,000cr
  • Middle Passage: 8,000cr
  • Low Passage: 1,000cr

To determine the number of available passengers, use the following table, with the following destination factors modifying the dice rolls when generating the number of potential passengers:

  • Amber Zone: -3
  • Red Zone: -6
  • Population 0-4: -3
  • Population 8 or more: +3

Keep in mind, characters may not be able to find passengers, or may not be able to find passengers able to pay for a higher rate of passage.

pages.name: Speculative Trade
pages.html:
Many travellers engage in speculative trade on the side to help pay off their debts and potentially make a profit while they are engaging in other jobs. The following steps outline the entire process of speculative trade:

  • Find a supplier: Find in starports or settlements.
  • Determine trade goods: Roll d66 on the trade table.
  • Determine the cost of trade goods: Roll 2D on the Cost Table.
  • The spacer then embarks on their interstellar trip to their next destination.
  • Locate buyer: Find in starports or settlements.
  • Determine sale price of goods: Roll 2D on the Cost Table.

Step 1) Find a Supplier

There are a few different types of suppliers to find. A result of 8+ is a success.

  • Legitimate supplier: 1D days in the starport to locate one; Broker check modified by SOC or EDU.
  • Illicit supplier: 1D days in the starport to locate one; Streetwise check modified by SOC or EDU. Illicit suppliers add +1DM to the D66 trade table to determine what goods they are selling.
  • Trade terminal supplier: 1D hours on a trade terminal in starports class A, B, or C. Admin Check modified by EDU. Requires a TL 8+ location.
  • Multiple suppliers: Travellers can look for multiple suppliers but incur a -1DM per additional lead they follow.
  • Starport modifier: DM+6 for Class-A, DM+4 for Class-B, DM+3 for Class-C.

Step 2) Determine Trade Goods

Use the following to determine each trade good a vendor is offering;

  • Number of different trade goods: All locations will offer a number of different trade goods equal to the location’s population code.
  • Common trade goods: All locations will have results of 11-16 on the trade goods table plus any of the other items associated with their location’s trade code, if the planet’s population number allows it.
  • Additional items: Each seller will have additional stock beyond what is commonly available. Roll d66 once to determine the trade good.
  • Apply the trade goods purchase DM if any. This is determined by the starport/settlement location where it is being purchased. Apply the DM to the price table roll.
  • For Example: A planet with population 9 that is Industrial will have all 11-16 items available plus 3 different trade goods that are available on Industrial worlds. All sellers will offer these goods plus one more that is randomly determined with a d66 roll.

The trade table is on the following page, pg. 54

Step 3) Determining the Purchase Price

Roll 2D and apply any of the following modifiers as needed:

  • Broker rank: The spacer’s broker Skill rank, or the broker Skill of any employed NPC broker.
  • Purchase DM: The Purchase DM of the trade goods, based on the location on the Trade Goods table.
  • NPC broker’s rank; Apply the selling NPC’s broker Skill as a negative DM. Professional sellers will have a Broker of 2, meaning -2DM.

Step 4) Locate a Buyer

Use the same procedures as Step 1 to locate a buyer.

Step 5) Determine Sale Price

Use the same procedure as Step 3, but use the Sale price column on the Purchase table to modify the 2D + Broker rank roll.

  • Negotiating sale price: if the initial sale price isn’t ideal, the spacers can negotiate. This is done in the same way as negotiating a purchase price, by determining the demeanor of the NPC, but every step increase is +1DM and every step decrease is -1DM to the negotiation roll.

pages.name: Hiring a Broker
pages.html:
Spacers can choose to hire a local broker to help them find and negotiate the purchase or selling of trade goods. Brokers can be found at the docks or carousing at taverns at any spaceport of C-class or higher.

  • Locating: A broker can be hired to find a willing supplier or news of soon-to-be-available supplies from a supplier in 1 week for 2Dx100cr.
  • Buying: The broker can be hired to provide an additional +1DM to +4 DM, +1DM for every 5% of the cost of purchase. For example, a Broker is willing to provide their Skill to a purchase negotiation at +2DM for a payment equal to 10% of the amount spent.
  • Selling: The broker can provide an additional positive modifier between +1DM and +4DM, +1DM for every 5% of the profits from the sale. For example, a broker is willing to provide their Skill to negotiate a sale at +2DM for a payment equal to 10% of the sale’s profit.

Incidentals

Starships that deliver to orbital starports are expected to pay for shuttle service to bring the deliveries planetside, equal to 10cr per ton. This is typical for very large starships that are not capable of atmospheric flight or for busy highports above high population planets with restrictive landing options or high atmospheric traffic.

Book p.65

pages.name: Price Negotiation
pages.html:
If the spacer doesn’t like the price offered, they can negotiate with the NPC.

  • Starting Cost: Determine the initial price for a product by rolling 2D and apply any Broker and trade good DM on the speculative trade table on the opposite page.
  • Trader option on Spacer: Roll 2D + SOC DM on the NPC interaction table on pg. 56 Apply the DM from that table. Apply this DM to future negotiation rolls between the spacer and trader.
  • Negotiate new price: To negotiate the purchase price, the spacer must roll 2D + Broker + NPC’s option DM and get an 8+ to get the NPC agree. The spacer can attempt to increase or decrease the price by determining the amount of steps on the purchase price column, which will be +DM for step decreases or -DM for step increases.

Example: Zolan wants to purchase bulk electronics to sell from a portside trader.

  • 1) The referee rolls 2D + Zolan’s Broker rank (1) and gets a result of 6 on the speculative trade table, meaning the trader is offering to sell the goods at 120% their average cost.
  • 2) Zolan attempts to negotiate, allowing for a 2D + their SOC DM on the NPC reaction table on pg. 56. Zolan rolls a 9 (the NPC is “Intrigued”), and this provides an additional +1DM when Zolan rolls to close the deal.
  • 3) However he must still lower the price, so Zolan says he will buy the goods at 80%, or 9 on the speculative trade table. This means Zolan will incur -3DM to this roll.
  • 4) To close the deal, Zolan rolls 2D + 1 (Broker) + 1 (NPC opinion) - 3 (counter-offer difference on trade table) and gets a total of 9. Success!

Book p.65
